title: GVR-ProtocolEval (repaired): Preregistered generate–validate–repair evaluation for NetOps safety across protocols and modalities
research_question: How much does a generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipeline reduce operational-failure rates (reachability loss or policy violation) relative to LLM-only generation, across protocol families and interaction modalities (CLI vs API), under controlled fault-injection?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: The GVR pipeline yields a lower operational-failure rate than LLM-only generation across the confirmatory task bank (paired comparison).
H2: Residual GVR failures will be concentrated in vendor-syntax translation and verifier-coverage blind spots rather than core logical errors.
H3: GVR gains vary by interaction modality: API-mode runs will show smaller residual failure rates than CLI-mode runs given identical verifier capabilities.
exploratory_questions: EQ1: How many repair iterations are typically required before verifier acceptance, and what is the distribution of iteration counts?
EQ2: Which specific syntactic translation patterns correlate with persistent GVR failures?
EQ3: How sensitive are primary results to verifier-rule coverage and to model nondeterminism controls?
benchmark_scope: Confirmatory custom task bank (200) of intent-to-configuration tasks executed in a Dockerized Mininet emulated testbed using public-domain vendor-syntax templates sampled from vendor documentation and RFCs.
Fault-injection scenarios limited to link flaps, device restart, and config drift emulated within Mininet containers.
Exploratory task set (50) for additional discovery analyses. Evaluations are bounded to emulated device behaviors and public vendor examples; no private production devices are used.
primary_estimand: Paired mean difference in the operational-failure indicator (1 if reachability loss or policy violation observed during deployment tests; 0 otherwise) between LLM-only and GVR pipelines, reported as absolute and relative reduction with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals (10,000 resamples, fixed RNG seed).
secondary_estimands: Per-protocol and per-modality paired mean differences (same metric as primary) with subgroup 95% bootstrap CIs.
Distribution and median of repair-iteration counts until verifier acceptance.
Proportion of failures attributable to syntactic-translation vs verifier-coverage blind spots (automated classification rules).
sampling_plan: Confirmatory task bank: exactly 200 tasks covering five protocol/focus categories (ACLs, static/dynamic routing, NAT, VLANs, service-ACL interactions) stratified across vendors and two interaction modalities (CLI, API). Allocation: 5 protocol groups × 2 modalities = 10 clusters; ~20 confirmatory tasks per cluster. Each confirmatory task is executed in a paired design across the two conditions (baseline LLM-only and guarded GVR) per the registered adapter contract. Exploratory: 50 additional tasks run for discovery. Task order randomized with fixed seed. Dockerized Mininet testbed seeded for deterministic fault-injection schedules. Inclusion/exclusion: tasks that trigger infrastructure errors (container crashes) are excluded from primary analysis but logged and reported separately; infrastructure failures treated as distinct from operational-failure outcomes.
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand power target: detect an absolute paired reduction of 10 percentage points (e.g., 30% → 20%) with 80% power at α=0.05. Power calculation uses a conservative paired-to-independent approximation with assumed within-task pairing correlation ρ≈0.5; resulting recommended confirmatory n=200 provides margin above the approximate required n≈145. Bootstrap CI method: 10,000 resamples with fixed RNG seed. Sensitivity analyses: recompute MDE with ρ∈{0.3,0.5,0.7} and baseline p1∈{0.25,0.30,0.35}. Per-cluster (n≈20) results are treated as secondary/exploratory due to limited subgroup power.
exclusion_rules: Exclude from primary confirmatory analysis any task run that experiences an infrastructure failure (container crash, Mininet fatal error); such runs are logged with reason and counted as 'infrastructure failures'.

Exclude and flag any generated configuration with >=80% token-level overlap to a single public-corpus document (treated in sensitivity analysis; excluded from primary analysis per contamination plan).
missingness_plan: If a deployed run fails due to infrastructure error (container crash, Mininet failure), log the run as 'infrastructure failure' and exclude it from the primary confirmatory binary outcome; report exclusion counts and reasons. Missing verifier logs trigger automated re-execution up to the preregistered retry limit (per adapter contract, retries limited to recover true infrastructure failures but not to obtain favorable scientific outcomes). All retained task outputs, including flagged/sensitivity items and exploratory runs, will be published with provenance hashes.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis: compute paired per-task differences in binary operational-failure outcome (LLM-only minus GVR). Estimate the mean paired difference with 95% bootstrap CIs (10,000 resamples, fixed RNG seed). Conduct Wilcoxon signed-rank test (two-sided) and report exact p-value for the primary hypothesis. Secondary analyses: compute subgroup paired differences with bootstrap CIs, describe repair-iteration statistics (median, IQR, histogram), and report automated failure-classification counts (syntactic-translation vs verifier-coverage). Apply Benjamini–Hochberg FDR control for secondary per-protocol subgroup tests (q=0.05). All analyses executed deterministically in Dockerized analysis code; raw artifacts and analysis code published to permit independent reanalysis. Label exploratory findings explicitly.
multiplicity_plan: One primary confirmatory test: paired LLM-only vs GVR on the full confirmatory bank (200 tasks). Secondary subgroup tests (per-protocol, per-modality) are multiplicity-adjusted using Benjamini–Hochberg FDR at q=0.05. Exploratory analyses reported unadjusted but clearly labeled as exploratory.
contamination_plan: Automated contamination detection: (1) exact-match and high-similarity checks versus a curated public corpus (vendor docs, RFCs) using deterministic string-hash and token-overlap thresholds; items with >=80% token overlap flagged and excluded from primary analysis; (2) automated similarity scoring (BLEU, longest-common-subsequence) between generated configs and corpus recorded and flagged when above thresholds; (3) publish all flagged items with provenance hashes. Residual uncertainty: unknown model pretraining overlap with public vendor examples cannot be fully ruled out; flagged exclusions and sensitivity analyses mitigate but do not eliminate this external-validity limitation.
stopping_rule: Execute each confirmatory task once per condition under the registered adapter contract. Stop when all tasks have been executed (200 tasks × up to 2 model calls = 400 maximum model calls under this contract) or upon exhaustion of the contract-specified maximum_model_calls (400). Log and report any early termination with reasons. No additional model calls or post-hoc extensions beyond the registered contract are permitted.
planned_outputs: Dockerized experiment code and CI unit tests (transformations, translator, verifier, Mininet harness).
Confirmatory and exploratory task bank (prompts, templates) with deterministic mapping manifest and hashes.
Raw model outputs, verifier logs, deployment traces, and Mininet testbed traces with provenance hashes.
Analysis scripts and deterministic outputs (bootstrap resamples, test statistics) in Docker.
Execution manifest and automated retry logs.
Evidence-to-claim table, nearest-work comparison matrix, and failure-analysis record.
IEEE-formatted five-page LaTeX manuscript draft and BibTeX bibliography (for CNSM special track), including mandatory Disclosure Statement.
NotebookLM presentation brief (machine-readable) summarizing question, method, main results, failure modes, and limitations.
